summary: The Jim Ovia Scholars Program, from the foundation of Zenith Bank's founder, gives about 100 new awards a year of N250,000 each to academically qualified, financially needy Nigerian undergraduates at federal or state universities, in any course. It is renewable each year if you reapply with proof of good grades. Winners are students with solid results, complete and perfectly prepared documents, and real financial need, who apply themselves within a very short window.
lookfor: Academic qualification: admitted to a Nigerian federal or state university, at least five O-level credits
Economic disadvantage - the programme targets youths in financial need
Complete, exactly-specified documents (a wrong or missing document disqualifies you)
Genuine records that pass verification - forgeries lead to blacklisting
Applying personally: no agents, one submission only
cycle: The form opens once a year between October and December for only a few days (18-24 Nov 2024; 26-28 Nov 2025). The 2026 window had not been announced when checked on 7 Oct 2026 - have every document ready by late October 2026. Decisions can take up to 20 weeks.

eligibility.q: Are you a Nigerian citizen living in Nigeria?
eligibility.no: The programme is for Nigerian citizens and residents only.

eligibility.q: Are you a matriculated full-time undergraduate at a Nigerian federal or state university?
eligibility.no: Postgraduates are not eligible, and the 2025 rules said federal or state universities. Look at other awards in Laureate Lab.

eligibility.q: Do you have at least five O-level credits (WAEC, NECO or GCE) with the certificate?
eligibility.no: You need the certificate itself. Request it from the exam body if it is not yet issued.

eligibility.q: Are you at least 16 years old?
Can you get a recommendation letter from your Head of Department, dated within the last four months?
eligibility.no: Ask your HOD early (see the References step). Without it the application is incomplete.

eligibility.q: Is your family in financial need?
eligibility.no: The programme targets economically disadvantaged students. If you are not in need, consider merit-only awards (SNEPCo, Seplat, MTN).

steps.title: Confirm you are eligible and understand the award
steps.why: The window is only a few days long. You must decide and prepare weeks before it opens.
do: Open the Jim Ovia Foundation FAQ and read it from top to bottom.
Open the 2025 new applicants page and read the rules list.
Check: federal/state university, five O-level credits, age 16+, full-time undergraduate.
Note the award: N250,000 a year, about 100 new awards, renewable only if you reapply each year.
tips: Any course can apply - there is no course list.
avoid: Thinking you can apply as a postgraduate - you cannot.
check: I meet every rule on the new applicants page.

links.t: 2025 application page for new applicants (closed; shows the rules)

steps.title: Learn the foundation's anti-fraud rules
steps.why: The foundation blacklists applicants who use agents, pay third parties or submit forged documents.
do: Bookmark jimoviafoundation.org. The form is only on that site.
Remember: no application fee, no agents, one submission per person.
Enquiries go only by email to enquiry@jimoviafoundation.org; the foundation does not take phone calls on applications.
If someone offers to 'apply for you' or 'guarantee' an award for money, refuse.
tips: The application is free. Anyone asking you to pay for a form, 'processing', a test slot or 'guaranteed selection' is a scammer.
Never use an 'agent' or cybercafe operator to apply for you with their email. Use your own email and phone so the funder's messages reach you.
Check any 'Jim Ovia' link: the address must be jimoviafoundation.org.
avoid: Letting a cybercafe fill the form with their email - this counts as using an agent.
check: I will apply myself, once, for free.

links.t: 2025 application page for new applicants (closed; shows the rules)

steps.title: Set alerts for October-December
steps.why: In 2025 the form was open for about three days. Missing it means waiting a full year.
do: Set a reminder to check jimoviafoundation.org every two or three days from 1 October to 31 December.
Follow the foundation's official social media accounts linked from its website.
Ask a classmate to check with you so one of you sees the opening.
Have all documents scanned by 31 October so you can submit on day one.
tips: Submit on the first day the form opens; sites slow down as thousands apply.
avoid: Waiting for blog posts - they often appear after the window has closed.
check: My documents will be ready before 31 October.

steps.title: Create a proper email address
steps.why: The rules say you must use a Gmail or Yahoo email that contains your first name and last name.
do: Create a Gmail or Yahoo address like firstname.lastname@gmail.com (add numbers if taken).
Make sure the names match your documents.
Turn on notifications and check spam folders.
tips: You may need to create a Jim Ovia Scholar's Account on the site when the form opens; use this email.
check: My email contains my first and last name.

links.t: 2025 application page for new applicants (closed; shows the rules)

steps.title: Get your ID, birth certificate and photo
steps.why: These are the first three items on the official checklist.
do: Get a recognised government ID (NIN slip/card, voter's card, driver's licence or international passport).
Find your official birth certificate (National Population Commission) or request one early if you do not have it.
Take a recent passport photograph and scan it.
Scan each clearly.
tips: A birth certificate can take time to obtain; start now if you lack one.
avoid: Using an age declaration where a birth certificate is required - check the current checklist.
check: I have ID, birth certificate and photo scanned.

steps.title: Get JAMB, admission and acceptance documents
steps.why: The checklist asks for your JAMB certificate/result, UTME result copy, university admission letter and acceptance letter.
do: Print your JAMB admission letter and UTME result from the JAMB portal.
Get your university admission letter and your acceptance letter (or acceptance fee receipt as issued by your school).
Scan your school ID card.
Scan your original WAEC/NECO/GCE certificate (not only an online printout).
tips: Check every name and date is readable in the scan.
avoid: Uploading only the online result when the checklist says certificate.
check: I have all JAMB, admission and O-level documents scanned.

steps.title: Get stamped results and the academic calendar
steps.why: The checklist is strict: results must be a signed and stamped student copy from first year to present, showing GPA per semester and overall CGPA.
do: Ask your department or exams and records office for a signed and stamped student copy of all your results so far, with GPA per semester and CGPA.
Medical students: ask for your grades converted to CGPA, with the university grading system attached, stamped and signed.
Get the current academic calendar, stamped or signed by the institution.
Scan both clearly.
tips: Write down exactly what the checklist says and show it to the officer so nothing is missing.
avoid: Submitting results without semester GPAs - the foundation says documents missing listed details are not accepted.
check: My results show every semester GPA and my CGPA, signed and stamped.

steps.title: Get your Head of Department's recommendation letter
steps.why: This is the only reference. It must be original, not older than four months, and show your current level, session, semester and CGPA.
do: Write a polite request to your HOD (in person if possible) in September/October.
Give the HOD a one-page note with your full name, matric number, level, session, semester, CGPA and a short summary of your financial situation and achievements.
Ask that the letter be on departmental letterhead, dated, signed and stamped, and that it states your level, session, semester and CGPA.
Collect it, check the date (within four months of the application window) and scan it.
tips: Ask for it in October so it is still valid in November-December.
Thank your HOD and tell them the outcome.
avoid: Using last year's letter - over four months old means rejection.
A letter that does not state your CGPA.
check: My HOD letter is dated within four months and lists level, session, semester and CGPA.

steps.title: Fill the form in one careful sitting
steps.why: Forms cannot be edited after submission, and a wrong document automatically disqualifies you.
do: When the window opens, go to jimoviafoundation.org and open the new applicants form.
Create your Scholar's Account if asked, using your name-based email.
Fill personal, contact, school and family details accurately.
Upload each document in the matching slot. Open each upload to check it.
If the form allows, print or save a copy before you submit.
tips: Use a laptop and a stable connection; have all scans in one folder.
avoid: Uploading the wrong file in a slot.
check: Every slot has the correct, readable document.

links.t: 2025 application page for new applicants (closed; shows the rules)

steps.title: Submit and keep proof
steps.why: You cannot edit after submitting, and you need proof if there is a problem.
do: Read everything once more, then submit.
Save the confirmation (screenshot or PDF).
Do not call the foundation; it does not take application calls. Email only if truly needed.
tips: Note the date; decisions can take up to 20 weeks.
avoid: Sending repeated emails asking for results.

steps.title: Wait for contact and track your account
steps.why: The foundation contacts selected applicants; the committee can take up to 20 weeks.
do: Log in to your Jim Ovia Scholars Account occasionally to check status.
Check email (and spam) weekly.
Respond quickly to any verification request with the documents asked.
Ignore anyone who asks for money to 'speed up' your award.
tips: Keep your HOD informed in case the foundation verifies with your department.
avoid: Changing your phone or email without noting it.
check: I know how I will be contacted.

steps.title: Renew every year as a returning beneficiary
steps.why: The award is not automatic. Scholars must reapply each year with proof of continued enrolment and good grades.
do: Each October-December, open the returning beneficiaries form on jimoviafoundation.org.
Get a fresh HOD letter (within four months) and updated stamped results.
Submit within the window like a new applicant.
If you were not selected, reapply next year with stronger documents.
tips: Keep a folder with each year's documents.
avoid: Assuming the money will continue without reapplying.
check: I have a renewal reminder set for October.

faq.a: N250,000 a year per beneficiary, renewable if you reapply and meet the conditions (per the official FAQ).
No essay was listed in the 2024 or 2025 rules or document checklist. Your documents and HOD letter carry the application. Check the current form in case this changes.
The rules ask for admission to a federal or state university and matriculation as a full-time student; check the current page for any level rule.
No. Enquiries go by email to enquiry@jimoviafoundation.org.

faq.q: Can a cybercafe apply for me?
faq.a: No. Using an agent can get you blacklisted. Apply yourself with your own name-based email.
No. It is for undergraduates only.
